subject: science
intro: Earth has four major systems that constantly interact. The geosphere is the solid Earth: rocks, soil, mountains, and land. The biosphere is all the living things: plants, animals, and other organisms. The hydrosphere is all the water: oceans, lakes, rivers, ice, and groundwater. The atmosphere is the layer of air around the Earth. These systems interact in many ways. For example, rain from the hydrosphere helps plants in the biosphere grow in soil from the geosphere, while wind in the atmosphere can wear down rock in the geosphere. A model with labeled parts and arrows can show how one system affects another.

items.prompt: A plant grows on a hillside. Which of Earth's four systems interact to make this possible, and how?

steps: The plant is part of the biosphere and grows in soil from the geosphere.
It needs water from the hydrosphere (rain or groundwater) and gases from the atmosphere (air).
So the biosphere, geosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere all interact to let the plant grow.
solution.answer: The biosphere (plant), geosphere (soil), hydrosphere (water), and atmosphere (air) interact so the plant can grow.

items.prompt: Wind blows across a desert and slowly wears down a rock into sand. Which two systems are interacting, and how?

steps: Wind is moving air, part of the atmosphere.
The rock is part of the geosphere.
The atmosphere (wind) acts on the geosphere (rock), wearing it into sand, so these two systems interact.
solution.answer: The atmosphere (wind) interacts with the geosphere (rock), wearing it down into sand.

items.prompt: A river carves a canyon into rock over many years. Identify the systems involved and the interaction.

steps: The river is water, part of the hydrosphere.
The canyon rock is part of the geosphere.
The hydrosphere (river) wears away and shapes the geosphere (rock), carving the canyon.
solution.answer: The hydrosphere (river) interacts with the geosphere (rock), carving a canyon.

They are the geosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere.
solution.answer: The geosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere.

items.prompt: Trees in a forest release water vapor into the air, which later falls as rain. Use the four systems to describe this interaction.

steps: Trees are part of the biosphere and the water they release is part of the hydrosphere.
That water vapor enters the atmosphere, then falls back as rain into the hydrosphere and onto the geosphere.
So the biosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, and geosphere all interact in this process.
solution.answer: The biosphere (trees) release water into the atmosphere, which returns as rain to the hydrosphere and geosphere.

items.prompt: Build a model showing how a rainstorm helps a farmer's crops grow. Label which system each part belongs to.

steps: Rain is from the hydrosphere and falls through the atmosphere.
The crops are the biosphere, growing in soil from the geosphere.
The model shows rain (hydrosphere) falling through air (atmosphere) onto soil (geosphere) to help crops (biosphere) grow, connecting all four systems.
solution.answer: Rain (hydrosphere) falls through the air (atmosphere) onto soil (geosphere) so crops (biosphere) can grow, showing all four systems interacting.
